tasks.description: Write the /task command at packages/core/commands/task.md (with byte-identical mirror at .claude/commands/task.md): every numbered behaviour in Intended Change, --resume, Decision rules (pointer only when no feature in flight; identify task by trd_file null plus kind task; notify before clearing pointer), Non-Goals, four-section readout, COMPLETE/STUCK banner, autonomy block.

In implement-trd step 1.2 (Branch-derived and Single in-progress), skip any implement.json whose trd_file is null or kind is task; mirror to .claude/commands/implement-trd.md; pin the text in verify-command-surface.test.js.

Register /task in docs and router: CLAUDE.md 21 to 22 commands; process.md and its template workflow line and reference entry; docs/reference/README.md rows; docs/reference/other-commands.md section; FRAMEWORK_HINT FLOW line in both router.py copies; router test assertion.

Pin task.md contract via describe block in verify-command-surface.test.js (criteria 2-7) and add task to mirror-parity list; add fixture test building a temporary task directory asserting recordResult persists deferred, session-context.js banner renders, status.js scan leaves directory unchanged.

could_not_verify: No live /task run. The command is a prompt, so whether a model following it runs each step once and writes every record is checked only by the functional-verification pass and the owner's first use. O1 and O2 are pinned by text and library behaviour, not by a live run.
The dart-repo observation in #52 is quoted from the issue, not re-checked.
open_questions: OQ-1: Should /task file its followups as issues in the project's tracker? Assumed No (filing belongs to the /ship-build design, #53). owner-only.

OQ-2: #52 says /task points current.json at itself. This plan does so only when no feature is in flight, and finds tasks for --resume by scanning instead. Assumed acceptable (narrowing justified by adversarial review). owner-only.
OQ-3: Should a task write its session log and dispatch ledger into its own directory? Assumed not in this change; they fall back to shared files. owner-only.
